      "emotionalDevices": ["shame"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Holland explains Grayling's disagreement through personal investment, potentially insulating his account by attributing resistance to bias. But he also supplies copying examples and a proposed genealogy of the disputed narrative (786–823). The motive attribution is unsupported here; it is unclear whether it overrides objections regardless of their merits."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1799,
      "endEvent": 1817,
      "contextStartEvent": 1651,
      "contextEndEvent": 1843,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "Yuma nism is so derivative of Christianity",
      "form": "yes",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["identity", "shame"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "After Grayling supplies non-Christian parallels (1749–1796), Holland calls their selection appropriation and reiterates Christian derivation. This may dismiss contrary examples without establishing their irrelevance. However, his preceding transmission argument and conference geography (1651–1745) supply reasons, and independent parallels do not themselves disprove a specifically Western genealogy."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 1941,
      "endEvent": 1943,
      "contextStartEvent": 1883,
      "contextEndEvent": 1947,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "I think you really want this to be the case",
      "form": "no",
      "substitution": "unclear",
      "protection": "unclear",
      "emotionalDevices": ["none"],
      "confidence": "medium",
      "explanation": "Grayling questions Holland's motivation without giving evidence for that diagnosis. It could deflect Holland's final genealogy claim by treating it as wishful thinking, but does not expressly make disagreement proof of a defect. Grayling previously offered counterarguments (1883–1897, 1925–1932); the closing exchange is brief and partly mixed."
    }
  ],
  "contrasts": [
    {
      "startEvent": 872,
      "endEvent": 882,
      "speaker": "A",
      "quote": "nor am i arguing that any period of history has been without its atrocities",
      "explanation": "Grayling expressly limits his thesis: earlier ethical reflection does not establish universal equality or humane historical practice. His ensuing examples of thinkers and traditions (883–993) support an argument about ethical ideas while preserving that distinction."
    },
    {
      "startEvent": 422,
      "endEvent": 433,
      "speaker": "B",
      "quote": "Christianity does not emerge in a vacuum",
      "explanation": "This compact formulation summarizes an explicit concession, supported by Paul's use of Stoic concepts. Holland then discusses Jewish, Persian, and Roman contributions (434–474), qualifying his claim that Christianity distinctively reconfigured inherited materials."
